subject: Cascade Health — Bakeoff plan, decision criteria, and next tests
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@cascadehealth.com>, procurement@cascadehealth.com
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@alphaai.com>, sales@nebulaserve.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Feb 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Cascade Health — Bakeoff plan, decision criteria, and next tests

Hi Ellen — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we stay aligned heading into the bakeoff window. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

High-level pain points you confirmed:
- Intermittent latency spikes on inference during 9am–3pm peak that cause UI timeouts for clinicians.
- Concern about auditability (per-request logs + immutable audit trail) for reporting & compliance.
- Need for predictable unit economics — finance needs a clear cost projection for 1M+ tokens/month.
- Data residency & HIPAA handling for certain PHI-containing prompts.

Goals for the bakeoff (what success looks like)
1) Latency: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 400ms for 512-token generation under simulated load.
2) Throughput: sustained 75–150 reqs/sec for baseline model inference with <10% tail degradation over 30 minutes.
3) Quality parity: outputs from candidate models must match clinical summarization baseline (F1 delta < 3 pts on curated prompts).
4) Audit & controls: per-request logs, searchable retention, and evidence of access controls.
5) Deployment flexibility: hosted + private (VPC) option and ability to pin model versions during rollout.

Competitive slate we discussed:
- Redwood Inference (us): focus on batching, KV cache, and private deployment options.
- AlphaAI: smaller vendor with fast model stack but limited audit retention.
- NebulaServe: promising cost profile; needs verification on quantization accuracy and KV behavior.

Open questions from our side (what we need from you)
- Confirm test dataset (anonymized clinical notes) or approve our synthetic dataset for initial runs.
- Procurement point of contact (procurement@cascadehealth.com is listed; please add name + phone).
- Any specific redlines required in the NDA — we can accelerate if you send a redline PDF.

Proposed immediate next steps
- I’ll send a bakeoff probe list (attached) and a sample test config for Redwood.
- Schedule a 3-day test window the week of Mar 8 for side-by-side runs (we can be flexible).
- Procurement/security will do a quick intake; we’ll run a short compliance checklist before any private deployment.

Attachments: CH_bakeoff-probes.xlsx (probe list + metrics), redwood-test-config.json (example), redwood-bakeoff-probe-list.xlsx (detailed prompts).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the proposed test window after you confirm procurement contacts and dataset.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@cascadehealth.com>

Cc: procurement@cascadehealth.com
Date: Wed, 23 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cascade Health — Bakeoff plan, decision criteria, and next tests

Hi Camila — appreciate the thorough recap. Couple quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Dataset: We can provide an anonymized subset of real notes (10k prompts) but we need a DPIA addendum before sharing. Can Redwood sign the DPIA addendum?
2) Success metric: For quality parity we use ROUGE-L in addition to the F1 you listed — can you include both in your scoring sheet?
3) Procurement contact: adding Marcus Li (marcus.li@cascadehealth.com) — he’ll handle procurement and contract questions.

Schedule: Mar 8 window works for us but can we do Mar 10–12 instead? That gives our security team two extra days to review the intake checklist.

Also looping in Tom Rivers from AlphaAI because they asked to understand the test dataset and timing (Tom — can you confirm if AlphaAI needs additional steps to receive the DPIA?).

Thanks,
Ellen
Director, Clinical Applications | Cascade Health
ellen.park@cascadehealth.com | +1 617-555-0199

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@cascadehealth.com>, Marcus Li <marcus.li@cascadehealth.com>, procurement@cascadehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@alphaai.com>, sales@nebulaserve.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Feb 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cascade Health — Bakeoff plan, decision criteria, and next tests

Thanks Ellen — Mar 10–12 is fine. We can sign the DPIA addendum; I’ll send the draft to Marcus and procurement and copy our legal counsel.

Updates & mutual action plan (timeline):
- Feb 24: Redwood sends DPIA draft + updated scoring sheet (ROUGE-L + F1 + latency/throughput booleans) — DONE (see attached).
- Mar 1: Security completes intake checklist and confirms dataset share protocol.
- Mar 4: All vendors receive anonymized dataset (or approved synthetic alternative) and test config.
- Mar 10–12: Side-by-side bakeoff (each vendor runs the identical probe set under the orchestrated load).
- Mar 15: Results review + decision recommendation meeting.

Detailed test scope (short):
- Latency/throughput under two traffic patterns: steady-state 100 reqs/s, burst 350 reqs/s for 60s.
- KV cache validation: repeated context prefixes to verify hit-rate improvements and tail latency behavior.
- Quantization sanity: measure delta in extractive summaries vs float baseline on a 200-prompt sample.
- Audit/retention check: vendor must demonstrate searchable logs with retention metadata and role-based access shown.

Attachments included: redwood-test-config.json, redwood-bakeoff-probe-list.xlsx (updated with ROUGE-L columns).

Tom/NeubulaServe/AlphaAI: please confirm you are good to receive the DPIA once Marcus signs off and whether you need a sandbox account prior to Mar 4.

Cc’ing Marissa for pricing and deal ops notes.

Hi Marcus/Camila — quick pricing note to help procurement plan budget: 

Proposed commercial bands for bakeoff and initial pilot (illustrative):
- Evaluation band (short bakeoff): no charge — we provide test credits up to 500k tokens per vendor.
- Pilot band (1–3 months): committed minimum $15k/month for reserved capacity with predictable throughput SLAs.
- Production bands: unit pricing tiers by qps and retention (we’ll share the CSV).

We can discuss a limited-time evaluation credit and a pilot discount in exchange for a 12-month pilot commit. Deal ID: D-CH-2027-042 (please reference when routing internally).

Next steps from pricing side: Marcus, if you can share target monthly token volumes and desired SLA (p95 latency target) we’ll return an initial commercial proposal by Mar 8.

Thanks — Marissa
